 Newlands hosts four-way fight for Pro20 Cup glory
 The Warriors, Boland, Lions and Cobras head to Newlands on Saturday with two wins separating each side from the Pro20 Cup trophy.
 After weeks of pool matches and Super 8 contests, the competition comes down to three games in a single day. The Warriors face Boland in the first semi-final before the Lions meet the Cobras, with the winners returning for the evening final.
 The Warriors finished top of the Super 8 standings, one point ahead of the Lions, with the Cobras third and Boland completing the semi-final line-up. Yet both fixtures offer a reminder of how little those positions might count: Boland have already beaten the Warriors in the Super 8s, while the Cobras did the same to the Lions.
 READ: Proteas and Bangladesh prepare for Highveld battle 
 The Warriors enter the weekend following a seven-wicket win over the Titans in Centurion. Jordan Hermann struck 95 off 53 balls and JP King added 56 off 33, sharing a second-wicket partnership of 146 to help chase down 181 with eight deliveries remaining.
 Matthew Boast’s 4-33 provided another encouraging sign. After conceding 26 in his opening over, the seamer recovered to make decisive breakthroughs, offering the Warriors a reminder of the value of sticking to their plans under pressure.
 Boland, though, have recent evidence that they can stop the tournament’s leading side.
 Their meeting at St George’s Park on 5 November finished level before Lizaad Williams took two wickets for two runs in the Super Over. Ferisco Adams then struck his first delivery for four to settle the contest.
 Williams had also delivered at the end of the regular innings, helping force the tie. His ability to execute when batsmen are looking for boundaries could again prove central to Boland’s chances.
 The second semi-final gives the Lions an opportunity to overturn last Saturday’s nine-run defeat at Newlands.
 ALSO: When De Zorzi made Bangladesh toil 
 Kashief Joseph’s 55 and Kyle Verreynne’s 46 off 22 balls helped the Cobras post 178-9 that evening. Richard Seletswane replied with 72, but the Lions finished on 169-6. For the hosts, that result provides confidence heading into another meeting at the same ground.
 The Lions responded by beating Boland by five wickets in Paarl on Wednesday, with Mitchell van Buuren’s unbeaten 60 guiding a difficult chase after they slipped to 49-5.
 Their spin pairing also made a valuable contribution. Bjorn Fortuin took 2-27 and Nqaba Peter 2-23, giving the Lions an effective means of taking wickets and restricting scoring through the middle overs. That contest with the Cobras’ batting order could be crucial again.
 Saturday will test each side’s depth and ability to adapt. The finalists must recover, reassess the conditions and produce again within hours. Four teams have earned that opportunity. By the end of the evening, one will have turned it into silverware.
